## API reminder

No complete chromVAR workflow was found in the source repository when this
template was created. This page is intentionally a minimal API reminder rather
than a validated analysis workflow. Check the current Signac/chromVAR
documentation before real use, especially for version-specific wrappers and
assay storage.
:::

## What it does

chromVAR estimates bias-corrected, per-cell deviations in accessibility for
sets of genomic annotations such as motif matches. Use it when the question is
cell-level motif activity variability, not enrichment of one selected peak set.

## Minimal current API

The current installed Signac 1.17.1 namespace does not export a
`RunChromVAR()` wrapper. The minimal direct chromVAR route is therefore shown
below. It starts from the motif-enabled assay created by
`motif_enrichment_findmotifs.qmd`.

```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(Signac)
  library(chromVAR)
  library(qs2)
  library(readr)
  library(tibble)
})

input_object <- "input/scatac_motifs.qs2"
output_scores <- "output/scatac_chromvar_scores.tsv"
assay_name <- "ATAC"

object <- qs2::qs_read(file = input_object)
stopifnot(inherits(object, "Seurat"), assay_name %in% Assays(object))
stopifnot(inherits(Signac::Motifs(object[[assay_name]]), "Motif"))

counts <- Seurat::GetAssayData(object, assay = assay_name, layer = "counts")
motif_annotations <- Signac::GetMotifData(object, assay = assay_name, slot = "data")
deviations <- chromVAR::computeDeviations(
  object = counts,
  annotations = t(motif_annotations)
)
scores <- chromVAR::deviationScores(deviations) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("motif_id")
readr::write_tsv(scores, output_scores)
head(scores)
```

## Outputs and decisions

`deviationScores()` returns motif-by-cell deviation z-scores; the bias-corrected
deviations are available with `chromVAR::deviations()`. Check that motif IDs,
peak IDs, cell IDs, genome build, and GC-bias/background calculations are
compatible. A motif deviation score is not proof of TF binding or causal
regulation.

Consult the current official Signac and chromVAR documentation for motif
matching, background peaks, bias correction, parallelization, and any updated
Seurat-assay integration before applying this reminder to real data.
